raw.assessment: The incumbent supplies a demonstrated assembly, an order-slip check and layout guidance: seven of ten customers succeeded unaided, and no damage claims were recorded. These observations do not establish completeness or attainment of the time target. Repeated three-compartment orders took seven to nine minutes, limiting the claim that full assembly necessarily causes excessive time; mixed batches could involve switching, intrinsically harder layouts or both. Overlapping widths among first-attempt and repeat insertions also weaken a width-only explanation without excluding tolerance interactions. The five customer reports do not distinguish packing errors from placement confusion.

openings.claim: Changing layouts between successive orders may increase selection and checking time beyond the intrinsic work required by each layout.
openings.delta: Tests sequencing while retaining complete workshop assembly, removable partitions and every accepted specification.
openings.prediction: For matched layouts and colors, interleaved sequences will have longer selection or checking times than blocked sequences; insertion times should change less.
openings.probe: Use up to 15 reusable samples. Have both workers assemble matched blocked and interleaved sequences, reversing sequence order between workers. Time selection, insertion, checking and packing separately; independently tally required parts. Compare within layout and worker. Before adopting sequencing, confirm the fixed dispatch schedule and cost caps remain feasible.
assumptions: Sample reuse does not materially alter insertion behavior.
Order sequencing can change without delaying accepted orders.

openings.claim: An exact ordered-layout diagram highlighting the short partition may resolve some unaided arrangement failures.
openings.delta: Replaces the three-layout illustration with order-specific placement information while retaining all product geometry and removable connections.
openings.prediction: With contents independently verified complete, customers receiving the exact diagram will ask fewer short-partition questions and complete more ordered arrangements unaided.
openings.probe: Randomize ten participants between existing and exact diagrams using verified sample organizers and balanced layouts. Record completion within ten minutes and placement questions. Treat results as exploratory; separately measure diagram preparation time and incremental cost before pilot use.
assumptions: The diagram can be supplied within the spending, recurring-cost and delivery limits.
Observed placement confusion responds to visual guidance.

raw.assessment: Two bounded hypotheses emerge from changing the unit of analysis. The observations do not identify the cause of missing parts, insertion retries, or long mixed-layout orders. Sample probes can discriminate mechanisms but cannot establish pilot success.

openings.claim: Represent each order as component-to-slot relations: an order-specific map and matching contents checklist may expose omitted roles during packing and clarify the short partition's destination during unpacking.
openings.delta: Replace the whole-organizer representation with required relations. Mark roles on the existing order slip and customer diagram. Recomposition rule: every required relation must have its physical partition present, and the complete map must reproduce the selected compartment count within the unchanged base.
openings.prediction: Compared with the generic diagram, fewer customers will request help locating the short partition; a role checklist will catch deliberately omitted or substituted sample parts before packing.
openings.probe: Use ten sample organizers and ten participants, five per diagram condition, balancing layouts. Record unaided arrangement, short-partition errors, and workshop checking time. On these samples separately test known omissions/substitutions. Cost the paper changes before pilot adoption; retain current slots, partitions, colors, and removable construction.
assumptions: Existing slips can carry legible role maps within both cost caps.
Added checking time is small enough to permit the eight-minute overall target.

openings.claim: Represent workshop work as transitions between order layouts. Layout switching may contribute to the long tail, making contiguous runs of matching layouts faster.
openings.delta: Change analysis from individual products to the order sequence. Recomposition rule: reorder work only; keep every accepted order's identifier attached to its parts and verify its selected count and exterior color before dispatch.
openings.prediction: For matched order mixes, grouped sequences reduce selection/checking time, especially immediately after layout changes, without increasing count or color errors.
openings.probe: Reuse the remaining five dismantlable samples for matched mixed and grouped sequences with both workers, reversing sequence order. Time selection, insertion, checking, and packing separately. Reject the switching explanation if phase times track layout difficulty rather than transitions. Adopt only a sequence that fits the fixed delivery schedule and existing budget.
assumptions: Accepted orders can be resequenced within the delivery date.
Sample reuse and practice do not dominate the measured difference.

openings.claim: Layout transitions may add selection/checking time beyond layout difficulty.
openings.discriminator: Within layout and worker, blocked sequences shorten selection/checking, especially after switches; insertion changes less.
openings.fit: Retains full assembly, geometry and removable parts; resequencing must preserve order identity, count, color and deadline.
openings.probe: Reuse five samples with both workers; reverse blocked/interleaved order, match layouts/colors, time four phases and independently tally contents.
openings.uncertainty: Intrinsic difficulty, practice and sample wear may explain differences; budget and scheduling feasibility remain unverified.

openings.claim: Order-specific component-to-slot maps may clarify short-partition placement; matching role checklists may detect packing omissions/substitutions.
openings.discriminator: Separate customer placement with verified contents from workshop detection of known missing/wrong parts.
openings.fit: Retains geometry, removable connections, selected counts and colors; added preparation/checking must fit cost, time and deadline limits.
openings.probe: Use ten samples and ten randomized participants, five per diagram condition, balancing layouts. Record unaided completion within ten minutes and placement questions/errors. Separately seed omissions/substitutions; measure checking and diagram preparation time and cost.
openings.uncertainty: Small exploratory sample; actual missing-part causes and response to guidance remain unknown.

lineage.reason: With A2; preserves phase-specific switching test.
With Z1; preserves transition timing and order identity.
With A1; preserves verified-content placement test.
With Z2; preserves separate role-checklist detection test.

post_distill.decision: Probe both; neither explains insertion retries or establishes pilot success. Preserve 30x20 footprint and assortment; confirm initial cost <=500, recurring addition <=0.40 and fixed delivery. Validate 60-unit completeness >=98%, median workshop time <=8 minutes and unaided arrangement >=90% before claiming success.
